title: They Just Wanna Be Loved
author: The Daily Dad
summary: This short Daily Dad meditation starts from the obvious observation that children differ in their tastes but share an appetite for things: toys, attention, treats and excitement. It then turns that observation around, arguing that beneath every request is a deeper and more uniform need. What children most want is to know they are enough, that they are safe, and that their parents are proud of them. The piece makes a pointed claim about the source of that love: nothing else is wanted more, and no one else's love is wanted more than a parent's. Its closing move is a direct charge to fathers not to ration affection or make children earn it, but to give it freely and immediately. Though brief, it states a clear parenting principle that fits the archive's Family bucket.
points: Children's surface requests for toys, treats and attention vary, but the underlying want is the same: to be loved.
The piece specifies what that love communicates: that a child is enough, is safe, and makes the parent proud.
It claims parents hold a unique place, since there is no one else children want that love from more.
The practical charge is not to withhold affection or make children fight for it, but to give it now.
quotes: Every kid is different. Every kid likes different things. But what they all have in common is that they want stuff.
Lots of it. Toys and attention. Affection and confections. Excitement…and expenses.
But you know what they really want, above anything else—even more than the stuff they ask for?
They want to know they’re enough. They want to know they are safe. They want to know you’re proud of them.
At the core of it, they just wanna be loved. By you—by their parents.
There is nothing else they want more and no one else they want it from more. So don’t hold it back.
